key_insight: AA-ViT uses anatomical, structural, and frequency guidance in a vision transformer to synthesize contrast-enhanced brain MRI from non-contrast scans while better preserving tumour and tissue boundaries.
clinical_relevance: If validated more broadly, this approach could reduce reliance on gadolinium contrast, shorten scan workflows, and improve access to contrast-like imaging when contrast agents are undesirable.
method: Uses pre-contrast MRI inputs: T1, T2, and FLAIR
Combines anatomical awareness with structure and frequency guidance in a vision transformer
Targets contrast-enhanced MRI synthesis with focus on boundary and lesion detail preservation
evidence_signal: On BraTS 2021, the model reportedly achieved higher PSNR and SSIM than prior methods and received a mean clinical rating of 3.94/5 from three neuroradiologists and one neurosurgeon across 19 randomly selected cases.
watch_item: The clinical validation is small and preliminary, so broader external testing and safety-focused assessment are still needed before real-world use.
paper_title: AA-ViT: Anatomically Aware Vision Transformer with Structural and Frequency Guidance for Contrast Enhanced Brain MRI Synthesis
